title: Tense and Reality
version: Modality and Tense: Philosophical Papers (OUP 2005), pp. 261-320; author-hosted PDF on Fine's NYU faculty page
relevance: Read in full (Spotlight extraction). Page mapping CORRECTED: anchor Savitt p. 306 = internal p. 72, offset +234. So book 304-305 = internal 70-71 = Fine's space/time-asymmetry discussion: spatial indexicality as frame-place pair, temporal as frame-time pair, every standpoint a standpoint of reality - the objection local fragmentalism must answer (O11 concession stands). The standpoint-chauvinism/arbitrariness argument is earlier (internal 63-67, book ~297-301). Independent of pagination: fn. 36 (internal 78-79) dismisses event-perspectives (Sprigge) as 'decidedly odd', assuming 'some more plausible way' - local fragmentalism claims to be that way, with R1 deriving what Fine left open; fn. 31: Fine's framework is 'essentially' Clifton-Hogarth's. Verbatim quotes: FINE_READING.md.
limits: PDF is the Equidox 'accessible' remake; quotes verified after whitespace normalization; book-page mapping rests on a single textual anchor (Savitt p. 306 = internal 72) - spot-check the print edition before quoting page numbers. Hofweber-Lange's quoted p. 308 phrase does not occur verbatim in this PDF (paraphrase, or from Fine 2006?) - see FINE_READING.md open questions.
locator: Sec. 9 (non-standard response; standpoints, internal pp. 63-74); Sec. 11 Fragmentalism (internal pp. 75-79); fn. 31 (Clifton-Hogarth, internal pp. 67-68); fn. 36 (Sprigge, internal pp. 78-79); 'Newtonian in structure' internal p. 72
assumptions: Non-standard realism about tense: tensed facts belong to reality without a privileged standpoint; SR forces reality to divide into frame-indexed or fragmented parts
conclusion: Fragmentalism is preferable to relativism within non-standard realism; times are not fundamental constituents, so relativity-to-a-time collapses; event-relative reality is dismissed as 'decidedly odd' (fn. 36) with the content of any event's reality left open
dependencies: Stein 1968/1991; Clifton & Hogarth 1995 (fn. 31); Sprigge 1992 (fn. 36); Putnam 1967; Godel 1949
open_questions: Whether Fine's 'more plausible way' remark plus fn. 36 concedes the conceptual space local fragmentalism occupies (our claim: yes)

title: The Fate of Presentism in Modern Physics
version: arXiv:1207.1490v1 (6pp, contributed essay); extracted in full
relevance: Upgrades the PRIOR_WORK 'snippet' entry. Names three fragment-adjacent proposals the novelty audit must check: (1) 'past-lightcone presentism' - 'suggested (but not ultimately defended) by Howard Stein (1991)' - cone-only coexistence, observed to break transitivity; note the stein-gr paper's Theorem 8 classifies any B with horismos-only steps as failing (T), so the paper formally explains this failure mode; (2) Harrington 2008 'point presentism' (spatially and temporally present only) - the strongest single-event-standpoint proposal; (3) 'private-space presentism' via Rindler 1981 public/private spaces - Wuthrich's cross-reality sentence ('those temporal parts of you which are real according to me-now take a temporal part of me to be real which is in the causal past of the me-now') is structurally close to local fragmentalism, though private spaces are hypersurfaces, not causal pasts. Also: Wuthrich cites 'Fine (2005, 304)' for the objective-now/no-objective-here asymmetry - independently confirming the corrected +234 page mapping. His objections to cone/private-space views (privilege of the here; no inter-observer agreement; extendibility; big-bang proximity) are pre-built objections the view's O-responses should absorb.
limits: Essay-length survey, not a theorem paper. Stein 1991 attribution of past-lightcone presentism needs verification against Stein 1991 itself (full text already in project). Harrington 2008 and Rindler 1981 not yet obtained.
locator: Sec. 4 (compatibilist modifications: Fine flow fragmentalism, past-lightcone presentism, Harrington point presentism, private-space presentism); Sec. 5 (incompatibilism: neo-Lorentzian, cosmological time, CMC); Sec. 6 (taking stock)
assumptions: Mild naturalism: no physically possible world is metaphysically impossible, possibility judged by best physics
conclusion: Presentism survives SR only at high cost (frame-indexed or fragmented existence, lightcone or point presents, private spaces, extra structure); Wuthrich judges all routes to bear costs too high
dependencies: Fine 2005; Stein 1991; Harrington 2008; Rindler 1981; Monton 2006; Wuthrich 2010; Tumulka 2006
open_questions: Verify Wuthrich's attribution of past-lightcone presentism to Stein 1991 against the Stein text already in project
